stem:
Ojas reads two 100 g nutrition labels for after-school snacks.

Potato wafers: 536 kcal, 35.0 g fat, 7.0 g protein, 4.8 g dietary fibre.
Roasted chana: 355 kcal, 6.26 g fat, 18.64 g protein, 16.8 g dietary fibre.

Which claim correctly identifies the junk-food pattern?

options.text: Potato wafers better fit the junk-food pattern because they are high in calories and fat and low in protein and dietary fibre.
Roasted chana better fits the junk-food pattern because it lists more protein and dietary fibre.
Dietary fibre (g) equals total carbohydrate (g) on every junk-food label.
The two labels cannot be compared because both are given per 100 g.

teacher.key_rationale: Junk foods are high in calories and fat and low in protein and fibre. Potato wafers match that pattern more strongly than roasted chana. Fibre is not the same as total carbohydrate, and same-mass labels can be compared.
